title: People Who Complain Incessantly About a Problem Before Addressing It
author: Admired Leadership
summary: The article profiles colleagues who habitually air complaints about a problem — and the people who caused it — before taking any action to fix it, arguing this pattern makes them exhausting to work with even when their eventual work is fine. It suggests the underlying motive is self-elevation: the gloomier the complaint, the more impressive the eventual fix appears to look. Using a vivid analogy of two plumbers — one who narrates every inconvenience before working, one who simply diagnoses and fixes the problem — the piece illustrates why colleagues quietly steer work and referrals away from chronic complainers. It closes by suggesting the plumber analogy itself as a tool for prompting self-reflection in a habitual complainer.
points: Complaining before acting is framed as a self-elevating habit: the gloomier the prognosis, the more impressive the eventual fix looks.
Colleagues quietly route work and opportunities away from chronic complainers, preferring not to 'stomach the negativity' even when the complainer's actual output is fine.
The two-plumbers analogy — one who narrates every inconvenience, one who diagnoses and fixes the leak — is offered as a memorable way to illustrate the pattern.
Confronting a habitual complainer directly is described as difficult but worth attempting, using the plumber analogy as a low-friction entry point.
quotes: Insisting on complaining about a problem (and the people who created it) before attempting to solve it is a mindset that fixates on what is wrong rather than how to address it.
By detailing the negatives surrounding the problem, these colleagues elevate their own self-worth and demonstrate to others how important they are in the process.
If given the option, they would prefer to work with someone else. They would rather not stomach the negativity and grousing that wastes time and drains others emotionally.
The second plumber arrives, examines the pipes, tells you what they plan to do, and then gets busy fixing the problem.

Convincing a complainer that they create an unproductive climate with their incessant whining isn’t easy. They have trained themselves to operate from this mindset, so it is difficult for them to grasp or make a change.
